facts.text: Bethania was founded June 12, 1759 by the Moravian Brethren of Wachovia as a congregational, agricultural, and trades community.
The town is the only remaining independent, continuously active Moravian village in the southern United States and the only known Germanic‑type linear agricultural village in the South.
Bethania’s 500‑acre historic district is the largest such district in Forsyth County and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
In 2007, the town opened the Historic Bethania Visitor Center, a museum that showcases Moravian life and the town’s 250‑year history.
The Wolff‑Moser House, dating to 1792, is one of the earliest surviving rural Moravian farmstead homes in North America and is open to the public.
Bethania celebrated its 250th anniversary in 2009, marking a quarter‑century of continuous settlement since 1759.
